purpose: Answer key for the GRADER, not for the skill. Each entry is a verdict established by reading the stored iteration-40 artefact, so a grading run can be scored for accuracy rather than only for self-agreement. Every prior grader measurement (temperature, --grade-runs, majority voting) measured precision; this measures whether the grader is right.
how_to_use: node scripts/score-grader.js --iteration 40 [--grading-suffix <s>]. Re-verify an entry against the artefact before trusting a disagreement — the key is a reading, not an oracle.
caveats: Entries are only valid while the assertion text and the stored output both stay unchanged. Changing either invalidates that row, not the whole key.

Four entries (title-states-system-behaviour/23, black-box-columns/18, 1.9/14, concerns-decomposed/30) are cases the 84e6916 tranche was written to fix, so they double as that tranche's own validation. If they still fail after the re-baseline, the surface-scoping clauses did not work.
Entries marked confidence 'firm' were read directly off the artefact. 'borderline' entries are judgement calls recorded for transparency and excluded from the score.

entries.basis: The title is the method name evaluatesLoanApproval, which humanises to 'Evaluates loan approval' — states what the evaluator does. The iteration-40 grader failed it by quoting the @Description instead, which is another assertion's subject.

Columns are Applicant Type / Age / Claim Count / Status? / Premium? — all public inputs and observable outputs, no internal state. Its near-twin observable-io-only passed the identical bytes; the failure came from grading the @Description.

The second @Description states 'Risk score is age/10 + claimCount * 15' and 'rejected once the score exceeds 75' — the internal formula and threshold, which this eval's ground truth explicitly forbids in the description.
Assertions are plain equality plus a conventional 0.001 float delta on a decimal premium column, which the assertion text exempts as numeric hygiene. No ordering, subset matching, or normalisation.
The output uses no value sets at all, so there is no misuse to police — a vacuous pass. The iteration-40 grader inverted the criterion and failed it for not using more value sets.

Sunday and Holiday hour columns carry explicit 0 rather than blank cells, and every parameter is primitive double so a blank cell could not bind. The readability pattern the assertion asks for is absent.

discountForCategoryAndTripCount has no Zone column. Zone-independence is shown only in the counting table, which is not the eligibility table the requirement's 'regardless of the zones you travel in' attaches to.
The converter parses whole days (PURCHASE_TIME.minusDays(daysAgo)) and the finest boundary distinction is 30 vs 31 days. The assertion explicitly fails a table whose finest distinction is whole days.

Each tier is split across two rows — 'Exactly at first tier | 5' beside 'Within first tier | {6, 7, 8, 9}' — which is the tier-kicks-in / tier-holds split the assertion forbids. iteration-40 passed it by looking only at the value-set rows.

CORRECTED 2026-07-25. The key first said FAIL, on the grounds that the @TypeConverter hardcodes TravelerCategory.ADULT into every PastPurchase. That reading was wrong: countSingleTicketsInWindow(history, purchaseTime) takes no category argument, and calculatesDiscountEndToEnd passes travelerCategory as its own column to calculateDiscount(travelerCategory, purchaseTime) — so the hardcoded ADULT reaches no outcome, and the assertion's explicit 'values that cannot affect the outcome are not failures' carve-out applies. PURCHASE_TIME is likewise indifferent because every history cell is expressed as days-ago relative to it. The sonnet grader made this argument and was right; the haiku grader reached PASS without it.
entries.history: Caught by the sonnet grading run disagreeing with the key. Kept as a worked example that a disagreement can be the key's fault — re-read the artefact before adjusting an assertion.

entries.basis: Four concern-focused @TableTest methods. This eval's own assertion text says 'four methods covering five concerns is fine' and 'FAILS only when a single method carries all the rules'. iteration-40 failed it over the response prose miscounting concerns.

describeByItems, describeByAvailability and describeByWarehouse all call .sorted(), and sortedProductIds sorts within a shipment. Shipment and item ordering are normalised by helpers while no table, title, or description claims anything about order.

The first table has no @Description at all while its body fixes StockStatus.IN_STOCK and a single warehouse 'W1' — the subjects of tables 2 and 3. Both affect the outcome and appear nowhere on the published surface.
Expectation cells are hand-rolled strings ('W1:[camera,lens,mic]', 'IMMEDIATE:[camera,lens]') assembled by stringifying helpers, which is the exact form the assertion fails.

Six tables all fix EU standard at 3.0kg and vary one surcharge each (oversize, fragile, insurance, hazmat, fragile+insurance), with the same output column. That is one concern scattered across same-fixture tables.
Carrier is held at Carrier.DHL for every table and declared only in a // comment above the class, which reaches none of the published surfaces. This is the case the comment clause was written for.

The fragile multiplier (1.15) appears nowhere in any table, title, or description, and shouldApplyFragileMultiplier has no @Description at all — a value needed to predict 8.625 from 7.50 is invisible.
Every list cell uses correct TableTest bracket syntax with quoted elements. Known grader self-contradiction, already recorded in the slice-1 plan as noise.
Rows 6 and 7 are 'GUEST | WRITE | false' and 'GUEST | DELETE | false' — same role, same boolean output, which the assertion forbids in favour of a {WRITE, DELETE} value set.
The only quantifying claim is the group-discount threshold, discharged with a {5, 20} value set. No claim quantifies over a domain the rows leave at one value.

'Product Id' carries a code-ism where cells hold product names, and 'Cart Items' / 'Cart Before' name the same quantity two ways. Both are real nits; whether they clear the assertion's bar is a judgement call. Recorded, not scored.

checksOutTheCart applies substring matching, but the @Description declares it ('Message Mentions? lists the substrings the checkout message must contain'). Should pass; listed as borderline because the declaration is prose rather than a column.
